newsitem.title: ISRAEL: CPI to take stake in Israel's Phoenicia.
newsitem.headline: CPI to take stake in Israel's Phoenicia.

text.p: Canada's Consumers Packaging Inc (CPI) will acquire 25.1 percent of Israel's Phoencia Glass Works Ltd as part of a strategic alliance, Phoenicia's parent, Koor Industries Ltd, said on Wednesday.

Koor said CPI would pay $4.35 million for the stake and transfer technology to the Israeli company to enable it to develop advanced glass packaging products. CPI will also help Phoenicia enter overseas markets, Koor said.
Phoenicia is wholly owned by Koor.

Koor managing director Benjamin Gaon said the agreement marked another step forward in the holding company's strategy of forming strategic partnerships with multinational companies in order to enter new markets.

In recent years, Koor, Israel's largest holding company, has fostered a series of similar strategic linkups for its group companies. Nortel is taking a 20 percent stake in Koor's Telrad Telecommunications and Electronic Industries Ltd, Volvo has acquired 50 percent of its Merkavim bus-manufacturing concern and Henkel 50 percent in Soad, a maker of personal-care products.

CPI, one of the world's leading companies in glass packaging products, has annual sales of about $500 million and operates seven plants in Canada and the United States. In December, it acquired a leading U.S. producer, Anchor Glass Container Corp, together with the U.S. concern Owens Brockway for $392 million.
Phoenicia has annual sales of about $30 million, Koor said.
